verdict: Avoid new readymade garment exposure in Bengaluru for now; lend only to domestic-focused, low-leverage job-work and made-ups units with tight monthly structure, and decline export-order-dependent and brand-led borrowers.
title: Bengaluru Readymade Garments & Made-ups: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
Pricing power is thin against large buyers, so margin is made on fabric sourcing and capacity utilisation. Collect from customer: fabric cost as share of sales, receivable days, and capacity utilisation. ## What has changed now
**National output is falling while bank credit to the sector is rising fast: IIP NIC 14 is -7.4% YoY and -5.6% Apr-to-date [D], yet bank credit is +23.3% YoY against that output fall [D].** Exports are -6.2% Apr-to-date in USD [D]. That gap means lenders are funding inventory and receivables that are not converting. Peer results split the same way: Raymond Lifestyle's garmenting order book runs to mid-Feb'27 with European traction [4], while Sangam's net profit fell to Rs.4.3 Cr in Q4 FY26 from Rs.12.8 Cr [5] and KKCL flags discretionary demand softness [6]. Local Bengaluru coverage is thin; the two local items are an online saree-sale cancellation [2] and a Rs.30 lakh fake-jeans seizure [3], so lean on first principles and peers here. ## Where to grow
**Pursue domestic-focused job-work and made-ups units supplying Karnataka's own retail and institutional buyers, and small units with a single anchor customer and no export dependence.** Avoid pure export converters and brand-led firms carrying high raw material and freight costs [4]. When a proposal lands, check the buyer mix; if more than half of sales are export orders, ask for the confirmed order book and buyer payment history before sizing the limit. ## How to grow safely
**Structure every limit as a cash-flow facility against verified invoices, not a clean OD, and take stock and receivable statements every month.** Set a drawing-power cap at a stated percentage of eligible receivables and inventory; collect from customer the exact percentage. Covenant a minimum current ratio and a debt-to-EBITDA ceiling, and take monthly stock statements, quarterly GST returns and buyer-wise ageing. If receivables age past the stated limit, stop further drawings until cleared. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch inventory days rising while sales fall, and receivables stretching beyond agreed terms, because that is exactly the credit-versus-output gap showing up at the borrower.** If a unit's order book shortens or a key buyer delays payment, cut the limit and move to invoice-backed drawing only. If GST turnover diverges from bank statements, treat it as a stop signal.
watch: Inventory days rise two months running -> freeze fresh drawings
Quarterly GST returns vs bank turnover
Gap over 10% -> ask for buyer confirmations and re-rate limit
Any invoice past agreed terms -> stop drawing until cleared
Order book shortens below one quarter -> reduce limit
Export share crosses half of sales -> require confirmed orders before enhancement
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Output -7.4% YoY and exports -6.2% while bank credit grows +23.3%, so funding outruns real sales.
